prompt: What are the three structural levels of a guided course?
explanation: A guided course groups curriculum into tracks, chapters, and short sequential lessons.

prompt: Which fields are required in the front-matter of a guided lesson? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Guided lessons require slug, title, topic, kind, summary, and goal. Author is not a recognized field.

prompt: How many bullet takeaways must appear in the Recap section?
explanation: The Recap section always contains exactly three bullet points summarizing actionable takeaways.

prompt: Put the standard sections of a task lesson in order.
explanation: Task lessons flow from Why you need it to Try it, How it works, and finally Recap.

prompt: Match each front-matter field to its purpose.

pairs.right: Old slugs redirected to this lesson

explanation: Each front-matter property serves a specific contract requirement in the guided format.

prompt: Which file defines the display order and lesson slug list for all chapters?
explanation: The content/topics.json file is the single source of truth for chapters and lesson order.

prompt: What is the maximum allowed reading time for a build lesson?
explanation: Build lessons allow up to 10 minutes (and 1500 words) to complete hands-on steps.

prompt: How many steps must a build lesson have in its Steps section?
explanation: A build lesson must contain at least two steps guiding the learner through construction.

prompt: In which track level is the "Going further" section allowed?
explanation: Going further is only permitted in tracks with level set to advanced.

prompt: What makes a good Going further section? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Pointers to language specifications and RFCs
Deep architectural trade-offs and edge cases

explanation: Going further provides deep dive context and references without burdening beginners.

prompt: What is the maximum character length for a lesson title?
explanation: Titles must stay concise and cannot exceed 60 characters.

prompt: Put the sections of a troubleshoot lesson in order.
explanation: Troubleshoot lessons present the symptom first, explain the cause, provide the fix, and recap.

prompt: Can a lesson title start with "Pitfall:" in guided format?

options.text: Yes, for any lesson teaching mistakes
No, titles must not begin with Pitfall

explanation: The guided format prohibits titles starting with Pitfall; use symptom questions or action verbs.

prompt: Match each lesson kind to its required sections.

pairs.right: Why you need it, Try it, How it works, Recap
Why you need it, How it works, Recap
What you'll build, Steps, Check your work, Recap
What you see, Why it happens, How to fix it, Recap

explanation: Each kind defines a tailored set of mandatory and optional sections.

prompt: What CLI flag enables strict release validation rules?
explanation: Passing --strict turns all pending warnings into release-blocking errors.

prompt: What happens if a quiz question references an alias instead of the current lesson slug?
explanation: Quiz questions must always point to canonical lesson slugs, never aliases.
